entry.title: До старту BPOL залишилося менше трьох тижнів — ще є час зареєструватися!
entry.content:
Найкращий спосіб зрозуміти, як працює бізнес — не читати про це, а побачити на власні очі.

У Business Processes Open Lecture студенти та викладачі матимуть можливість отримати доступ до навчальних матеріалів, зайти в реальну систему SAP S/4HANA і відпрацювати процеси самостійно.

Плюс — офіційна сертифікація SAP наприкінці програми. Старт 5 листопада, реєстрація ще відкрита.

📌 Business Processes Open Lecture 2026/27 (BPOL) — це 60-годинна навчальна програма від SAP для студентів і викладачів акредитованих університетів.

| Що на вас чекає:

  • 38 годин самостійного навчання у SAP Learning Hub — у зручний для вас час
  • 21 жива Zoom-сесія щотижня (четвер, 17:00–18:00 CET) з експертом SAP
  • Доступ до реальної системи SAP S/4HANA — практичні вправи в живому середовищі
  • Офіційний іспит SAP Certification — 2 безкоштовні спроби від SAP
  • Реєстрація — безкоштовна

| Як зареєструватися:

Сайт реєстрації — універсальна платформа SAP, тому деякі поля можуть здатися незрозумілими. Ось що обирати:

  • Industry → Higher Education & Research
  • Relationship to SAP → Student
  • Function → Delegate
  • Business email → ваш університетський email (обов’язково — підтверджує право на участь)
  • Company → назва університету англійською (можна вводити вручну)
  • Department → будь-який з переліку

Вибір опцій не впливає на статус реєстрації — головне, академічний email.

| Ведуть програму:

  • Dr. Michael Nürnberg — Global Head Academic Partner Success, SAP University Alliances
  • Prof. Dr. Christoph Bode — Chair of Procurement, University of Mannheim
  • Dr. Tamas Szirtes — Group Innovation Director & SAP Mentor, SOA People
  • Sophie Windisch — Working Student, SAP University Alliances
  • Mikka Bongard — Working Student, SAP University Alliances

👉 Зареєструватися

entry.title: Know an SAP Champion: My Conversation with Mustafa Bensan about AI at SIT Porto 2026
entry.content:
At SAP Inside Track Porto 2026, one session stood out for me: Mustafa Bensan’s presentation on SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise vision. After the session, I took the chance to introduce myself and talk with him about AI.


With SAP Champion Mustafa Bensan at SAP Inside Track Porto 2026

Who is Mustafa?

Mustafa is an SAP Champion and the founder and Chief Architect of Intentum, with more than 30 years of experience on SAP projects around the world. What I found encouraging is that he started his career as an ERP functional consultant, like many of us, before moving into analytics and architecture.

What impressed me in his session

Mustafa’s presentation went into much more detail, including a full live demo. Here I’m sharing just a few points that stood out to me as a finance consultant.

The highlight was a live voice demo. Mustafa simply spoke to an AI voice agent, and the agent responded to him in real time. No searching for transaction codes, no navigating through screens: you speak, and you get an answer.

The voice agent was built on the LiveKit platform, and the demo was inspired by SAP’s partnership announcement with LiveKit at SAP Sapphire Madrid. Seeing it live made the idea of the “Autonomous Enterprise” feel much less abstract. Instead of users having to know where to look in the system, they can simply ask.

What we talked about

After the session, we talked about where AI is heading in SAP and what it means for the people who work with these systems every day. For me, it was valuable to hear the perspective of someone who has seen so many technology shifts in SAP over three decades.

What it meant to me

As an SAP FICO and Joint Venture Accounting consultant, my first thought was about finance. If a user can simply ask a question and get an answer, finance work like checking balances, investigating postings or preparing for the month-end close could become much faster, especially for business users who don’t know every report and transaction code.

But in finance, an answer is only useful if it’s correct and you can trace where it came from. Finance teams are rightly careful about where their data goes and where their numbers come from. So for me, the key questions for any AI assistant in finance are: which data does it use, how is that data secured, and can the user verify the answer?

That’s where finance consultants continue to play an important role: making sure the data behind the answers is right, that the right controls are in place, and that users know how to check what they’re told.

My takeaway

I came away more curious than worried. Conversational AI will change how we work with SAP, and I want to understand it early, especially how it can support finance processes in a trusted and controlled way.

Thank you, @MustafaBensan , for taking the time to talk with me, for a session that made the future of SAP feel very real, and for kindly clarifying the details of the demo afterwards. And to anyone attending an SAP event: don’t hesitate to approach an SAP Champion. One short conversation can give you a lot to think about.

#KnowAChampion #CatchAChampion #SAPCommunity #SAPChampions

This post was assisted by GenAI. The experiences and opinions are the author’s own.

entry.title: HighRadius vs. SAP FSCM: Hard-Earned Lessons from a Global Cosmetics S/4HANA Transformation
entry.content:
As consumer goods and beauty organizations accelerate their digital finance transformations, the debate surrounding Accounts Receivable (AR) optimization often gets reduced to a binary question: Should we use native SAP Financial Supply Chain Management (FSCM) or replace it with a specialized cloud solution like HighRadius? Over an 18-year career leading global SAP transformations across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, I have watched finance executives repeatedly fall into the trap of treating this as an "either/or" software selection choice.

The reality on the ground is completely different. When you move past the product brochures and slide decks, you discover that the most successful global templates do not choose between them. Instead, they treat SAP as the core transactional engine and HighRadius as an intelligent edge layer. Achieving this coexistence, however, requires navigating complex architectural integration points, version-specific database behaviors, and industry-specific commercial nuances—such as complex trade promotions and massive retail deductions—that software vendors rarely mention during the sales cycle.

The Friction Point: Why Pure SAP FSCM Fell Short in Global Beauty & Cosmetics Rollouts

To understand where native capabilities hit their limits, we can look at a global cosmetics leader's rollout running on an SAP S/4HANA 2023 On-Premises environment with Feature Package Stack 02 (FPS02). The business model managed a deeply fragmented customer landscape: massive multinational retail networks (such as Sephora, Ulta, and major department stores), thousands of highly localized salon accounts, and high-volume e-commerce payment clearing.

Initially, the steering committee pushed for a pure SAP FSCM Collections and Dispute Management implementation to minimize their software footprint and leverage their existing licensing. However, as we entered the blueprinting and prototyping phases, the operational limitations of a purely rule-based system in the cosmetics industry became apparent:

  • The Trade Promotion Deduction Avalanche: Major retail beauty chains routinely short-pay invoices based on cooperative advertising agreements, volume rebates, and markdown allowances. In standard SAP FSCM, these deductions flood the subledger as individual residual open items. Dispute specialists spent up to 40% of their day manually linking these short payments to promotional agreements, creating a massive operational backlog.
  • Static Collection Strategies: SAP FSCM generates collection worklists based on static, pre-defined rules—such as aging buckets, risk categories, and total open values. In a fast-moving retail consumer landscape, these rigid rules created bottlenecks. The system flooded collection specialists with alerts for large, stable retail accounts that routinely paid according to strict corporate payment cycles, while high-risk, deteriorating independent salon behaviors slipped through unnoticed because they hadn't crossed a specific net-due threshold.
  • The Analytics Deficit: Standard SAP operational reporting (even via custom operational data provisioning views or standard Fiori FES 2023 apps) provided lagging operational KPIs. The business leadership lacked predictive cash forecasting and granular, dynamic Day Sales Outstanding (DSO) trend analysis segmented by shifting channel behavior patterns (D2C vs. B2B Wholesale).

The organization realized that while FSCM was perfectly engineered to maintain the financial integrity of the ledger, it lacked the algorithmic agility needed to optimize cash application hit rates and automatically resolve multi-brand deduction claims. This realization shifted our strategy to a hybrid architecture deploying the HighRadius Cash Application Cloud and Deduction Management System (DMS) modules alongside our SAP core.

Architectural Reality: Orchestrating Integration via Hyperion Integration Platform (HIP)

Integrating a multi-entity S/4HANA 2023 core with a cloud-based Autonomous Finance platform is rarely a "plug-and-play" exercise. For this transformation, we built a hybrid ecosystem where SAP functioned strictly as the immutable system of record, while HighRadius operated as the system of engagement and intelligence, orchestrated via the Hyperion Integration Platform (HIP) as the corporate middleware layer.

The underlying architecture relied on standardizing data exchange protocols across an enterprise footprint. Because the corporate landscape utilized HIP as its centralized enterprise middleware, we funneled all transactional deltas, ledger extract files, and incoming bank lockbox information through this layer to perform essential schema transformations before delivering them to High Radius.

The technical complexity surfaced heavily during the orchestration of the data loop between HighRadius Cash App, DMS, and SAP FI-AR via HIP:

  1. The Cash App Ingestion: HighRadius Cash App automatically extracts unstructured remittance data via OCR from customer emails and retail vendor portals, matching payments against open customer line items. This open item subledger data is periodically extracted from SAP operational views (such as BSID) and delivered through HIP as a structured outbound file payload.
  2. The DMS Splitting Mechanism: When a retail client short-pays an invoice due to a trade promotion dispute, the Cash App module flags the variance and automatically routes the residual shortage amount to the HighRadius DMS module.
  3. Automated Inbound Postings through HIP: Once a deduction is classified in the cloud, HighRadius communicates the clearing parameters back down. HIP intercepts this response payload, translates the cloud parameters into SAP-compatible structures, and executes an inbound transactional interface leveraging standard functions like BAPI_ACC_DOCUMENT_POST. This automatically clears the original invoice line item in S/4HANA, posts a residual open item for the short-payment, and maps specific SAP Reason Codes corresponding to the dispute type (e.g., Pricing, Shortage, or Coop Ad).

By utilizing HIP as the unified integration layer, we eliminated complex point-to-point interface sprawl, ensuring that our daily cash application cycle remained decoupled from the extended timelines required to research and settle retail trade promotions.

Version Constraints and Unexpected Implementation Roadblocks

Moving from conceptual architecture to actual deployment on S/4HANA 2023 (FPS02) exposed several technical constraints that project planners frequently overlook.

Our first major hurdle involved the Universal Journal (ACDOCA). In older SAP ERP Central Component (ECC) environments, financial data was highly segmented across index tables (like BSID and BSAD). S/4HANA’s unified ACDOCA design vastly speeds up internal reporting, but extracting massive delta datasets of open and cleared items to feed external machine learning models can degrade system performance if not carefully managed.

During initial data cycles, our delta extraction queries for historical customer payment behaviors began causing severe memory bottlenecks in the SAP HANA database due to the sheer volume of line items generated by cosmetic wholesale shipments. We had to configure the SAP extraction jobs and HIP to abandon generic open-ended queries and completely redesign our extraction logic. We restricted data pulls to strict timestamp-based delta captures leveraging specialized SAP Change Data Capture (CDC) mechanisms, ensuring that data replication to HighRadius occurred in controlled micro-batches outside of peak financial closing windows.

Another critical constraint appeared within the Business Partner (BP) master data synchronization. Because this was a global program spanning multiple geographies and brands, the client utilized complex BP groupings with varying field modification rules across different company codes. HighRadius requires a highly standardized payload for its ingestion models.

We encountered repeated integration errors where localized fields in SAP (such as specific regional tax classification rules or localized payment block reasons) caused data validation rejections in the HighRadius staging tables. This required a comprehensive data-cleansing initiative and configuring specialized transformation rules within HIP to map heterogeneous SAP BP attributes into a unified schema that the HighRadius machine learning algorithms could accurately interpret.

The Measurable Bottom Line: Concrete Project Outcomes

The true validation of this hybrid architectural strategy lies in the quantifiable business results achieved in 12 months of post-go-live. By shifting from static, rule-based workflows to an AI-driven, predictive model, the global shared services organization transformed its balance sheet performance:

 

The dramatic leap in our auto-cash application hit rate was particularly impactful for the consumer goods model. By leveraging HighRadius’s OCR and machine learning algorithms to automatically parse unstructured remittance advices from customer emails and retail vendor portals, the system matched payments to open items in S/4HANA without human intervention. This freed up our senior credit analysts to focus exclusively on negotiating complex promotional shortages rather than manual data entry.

Strategic Recommendations for Enterprise Architects Today

If I were to approach a global cosmetics architecture rollout again today, I would change my implementation strategy in two distinct areas:

  1. Mandate Early-Stage Data Cleansing: Do not wait for the integration testing phase to discover that your SAP Business Partner master data or customer hierarchies are inconsistent across regions. Master data remediation must be treated as a strict technical prerequisite that runs six months before any external cloud integration work begins.
  2. Enforce the Transactional Boundaries Immediately: Be incredibly disciplined about keeping business logic where it belongs. Cloud platforms will tempt you to build complex custom validation workflows or store trade promotion contracts within their environments. Resist this pressure. All accounting principles, credit limits, and final clearing rules must reside strictly within the S/4HANA core to protect your financial system of record. Use the HIP-enabled cloud edge purely for execution speed, prediction, and user experience.

Ultimately, the choice between SAP FSCM and HighRadius is a false dichotomy. The real challenge—and the real opportunity for enterprise architects—lies in configuring a robust, high-performing integration framework that respects the transactional authority of SAP while fully unleashing the analytical power of autonomous finance.

Author Bio

Prakashreddy Bodireddy is an SAP S/4HANA Certified FICO Solution Architect with 18+ years of experience delivering global finance transformation programs across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and the Americas. His expertise includes SAP S/4HANA Finance, FSCM,  Group Reporting, IFRS15/RAR, Treasury, and HighRadius integration.

entry.title: From SAP TechEd Berlin to Your Next Blog Post
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community!

I’m Fatemeh Zarei, and I’ve been working with the SAP Community team for over a year now, creating content and helping share stories from across the community.

During this time, I’ve had the opportunity to attend D-COM and SAP Inside Track Hamburg. Attending SAP Inside Track Hamburg gave me the opportunity to enjoy interesting sessions and connect with fellow community members. I’ve always loved events for exactly this reason: the chance to exchange ideas and get to know the people behind the technology. That experience helped me better understand SAP technology and connect with the great SAP community in Hamburg.

That’s also why I enjoy hearing people’s stories after an event. We can attend the same event and come away with completely different experiences. A session you almost skipped might become your biggest takeaway, or a quick conversation might introduce you to someone you’ll stay connected with.

So, why not share your upcoming SAP TechEd Berlin experience with the SAP Community?

You don’t need to be an experienced blogger, and you don’t need to write about everything that happened. A few highlights, useful lessons, or memorable community moments are a great place to start.

Let’s go!

Your SAP TechEd Story: 10 Questions to Get You Started

Use some of the questions below as a starting point for your blog post draft. Choose the ones that are meaningful to you, skip the others, and add anything else you’d like to share.

Who are you, and what brought you to SAP TechEd?

Introduce yourself briefly. Tell readers about your role, your interests, and whether this was your first SAP TechEd.

What were you most looking forward to, and how did the experience compare?

Perhaps you wanted to explore a particular technology, get hands-on experience, or meet fellow community members. Tell us how it went and what surprised you.

Which session stood out to you, and why?

Share what made it worth attending and your main takeaway. Include a link to the session or related resources so readers can explore further.

What technology or idea are you excited to explore further?

Whether it’s SAP Business AI, Joule, application development, integration, or something completely different, tell us what caught your attention and why.

What did you learn that you could apply in your work?

Describe a practical tip, a new approach, or an idea you’d like to try with your colleagues, customers, or projects.

Did a session or conversation change your perspective?

Tell us what you thought before and what made you see things differently. It could be a technical insight or something you learned from another person’s experience.

Who did you connect with, and what made that interaction memorable?

Maybe you met someone you previously knew only online, reconnected with a community friend, or had an unexpected conversation. Share what made that connection special and tag the people you met so they can join the conversation. If you took a picture together, consider including it, with their permission of course 🙂

What was your favorite SAP TechEd moment?

Choose one moment that captures the event for you. If you have a picture, include it and tell us the story behind it: what was happening, who you were with, and why it mattered.

What advice would you give a first-time attendee?

Share a practical tip you wish you’d known beforehand—whether it’s about choosing sessions, preparing for the event, or making time for community activities.

What comes next?

Tell us what you plan to do with what you learned. You might try a new technology, share your takeaways with colleagues, stay in touch with someone you met, or create your next SAP Community contribution.

Now It’s Your Turn! ✨

Your blog post doesn’t have to follow this exact order or answer all ten questions. Choose the ones that help you tell your story and add pictures and useful links along the way.

Before publishing, complete the Tour the SAP Community tutorial if you haven’t already, it’s required for blogging and will help you get familiar with the platform before sharing your story.

Ready to share? Create your blog post in Community Corner and add the SAP TechEd and SAP Community tags so others can find your story.

Finish by inviting readers to join the conversation. You could ask: “What was your biggest SAP TechEd takeaway?”

Most of all, write in your own voice. Your experience and perspective are what make your contribution worth reading.

I’m looking forward to reading your SAP TechEd stories and discovering the sessions, people, and moments that made the event special for you!

Have fun blogging!

Цього року — 140+ сесій за три дні: реальні кейси, hands-on лаби, демо та пряме спілкування з SAP-продуктовими командами. Захід відкритий для всіх, хто хоче дізнатися більше про SAP Application Lifecycle Management — незалежно від досвіду чи ролі.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026 — Day 1: O Resumo que Você Precisa Ler
entry.content:
Salve, comunidade CWB!

Luiz Souza por aqui! Esse ano consegui encaixar na agenda para acompanhar o SAP TechEd 2026 pelo virtual — de Curitiba mesmo, café na mão e duas telas abertas. E valeu cada minuto. O Day 1 já veio carregado e trouxe aqui os destaques para quem não pôde assistir (ou assistiu e quer um resumo rápido). Vem comigo!

🕐 Update do futuro: Voltei do Day 2 e posso confirmar — ficou ainda melhor. Robôs autônomos, IA no espaço e 300 agentes prontos pra uso. Após ler o artigo completo, Não perca: 👉 Leia o resumo do Day 2 aqui


O que aconteceu hoje em Berlim?

O SAP TechEd 2026 começou hoje em Berlim e o primeiro dia já veio carregado. O evento vai até quarta-feira (29/10) e pode ser acompanhado de graça na versão virtual. Aqui vai o resumo do Day 1 para quem quer ficar por dentro sem precisar assistir tudo.

 

O Developer Garage 

Logo no começo da transmissão do SAP Developer News, a gente já vê o Developer Garage — aquele espaço hands-on onde o pessoal senta, abre o laptop e sai testando as novidades com zero pressão. Tutoriais prontos, ferramentas carregadas e os Developer Advocates ali do lado ajudando. Confesso que deu uma inveja boa de quem estava lá presencial.

 

Um "guardião" para toda a IA da empresa

Essa parte me chamou atenção assistindo a cobertura: a SAP anunciou o SAP Enterprise AI Gateway — basicamente um painel de controle central para tudo que envolve IA na empresa. Quem acessa o quê, quais modelos estão rodando, quanto está sendo consumido e se está tudo dentro das regras.

Faz sentido: quando a empresa começa a usar vários agentes e modelos de IA ao mesmo tempo, o risco de perder o controle cresce. O gateway resolve isso com uma camada única de segurança, monitoramento e auditoria. Funciona com protocolos abertos (MCP e A2A), então agentes de diferentes fornecedores podem trabalhar juntos sem perder a governança. Planejado para Q1 2027.



A IA da SAP agora faz, não só sugere

A keynote foi o ponto alto da transmissão. A frase que ficou: a SAP está passando de uma IA que aprende o negócio para uma IA que opera o negócio.

O Joule Work é o melhor exemplo disso. Você descreve um objetivo e agentes de IA planejam os passos e executam tudo no landscape SAP, de ponta a ponta. Assistindo de casa, deu pra sentir a energia do auditório quando mostraram isso ao vivo.

Outro momento que parei o café pra prestar atenção: o SAP-RPT-2.0, modelo de IA para dados estruturados, agora detecta anomalias automaticamente e faz previsões de negócio sem precisar de um projeto de ML do zero. E em parceria com a HPE, esse modelo foi levado para a Estação Espacial Internacional — sim, rodando a bordo, prevendo falhas em equipamentos sem enviar dados de volta à Terra. Ficção científica virou realidade.

Bônus: a certificação Joule Studio Developer está gratuita até 31 de dezembro de 2026. Já anotei aqui.

ABAP está mais vivo do que nunca

Como alguém que vem do ABAP clássico, essa parte me pegou. O recado foi claro: o ABAP não vai embora — ele está evoluindo com IA.

O ABAP MCP Server permite que qualquer ferramenta de IA interaja diretamente com sistemas ABAP. O desenvolvimento em VS Code ganha suporte cada vez maior. E o SAP-ABAP-1, modelo de IA treinado no código ABAP da própria SAP, já está disponível para ajudar a escrever código, gerar testes e acelerar migrações.

Para quem, como eu, está na jornada do clássico para o moderno: as ferramentas que vão turbinar nosso dia a dia estão chegando — e muitas já estão disponíveis.

Amanhã tem mais — e você também pode assistir

O Day 1 foi só o começo. Amanhã (28/10) continua com sessões técnicas, workshops e mais anúncios — incluindo a noite de celebração dos 30 anos do SAP TechEd.

Eu vou estar acompanhando de novo pelo virtual e trazendo os destaques. Se você ainda não se registrou, a versão online é gratuita e dá acesso às keynotes ao vivo e ao conteúdo on demand depois.

👉Registre-se para o SAP TechEd Virtual (gratuito)

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026 — Day 2: Agentes, Robôs e 30 Anos de TechEd
entry.content:
Hello Everyone!   

Inglês bombando na mente por aqui, mas segue o resumão!!!

Se você perdeu o Day 1, fiz um resumo com os principais anúncios: SAP Enterprise AI Gateway, o modelo SAP-RPT rodando na Estação Espacial, novidades para ABAP e a certificação Joule Studio gratuita. Leia o resumo do Day 1 aqui

Agora bora pro Day 2, que veio ainda mais intenso.

Pega o café e vem comigo! 


Antes de tudo: palmas pro Kasimir 🐱🕶️

Eu preciso começar elogiando o time de marketing da SAP. A abertura da Developer Keynote foi um curta-metragem cinematográfico estrelado pelo @josh_bentley  e Kasimir — ou melhor, Agent v0.0.7 (perceberam o trocadilho com 007?). Um gato animado de smoking e gravata borboleta, em uma paródia de James Bond chamada "A License to Skill". Contagem regressiva dos 30 anos, mapa digital de Berlim, entrada dramática na névoa, o diamante do Joule brilhando no céu e até um disquete de mármore — porque a SAP não esquece de onde veio.

O vídeo é curto, divertido e resume perfeitamente o espírito do evento: tecnologia séria com personalidade. Se você não viu, assista aqui a abertura completa — vale cada segundo.

 


 


IA que faz o trabalho por você

O Joule Work ganhou uma nova cara: interface redesenhada, conectado de fábrica ao Office 365, ServiceNow e outras ferramentas, e disponível no celular, desktop, voz e até no CarPlay da Apple. Ele agora lembra suas preferências e se adapta ao longo do tempo.

Mas o número que chamou atenção foi outro: a SAP anunciou 40 assistentes e 300 agentes prontos para uso, cobrindo finanças, compras, RH, supply chain e atendimento ao cliente. Todos certificados ISO e SOC — ou seja, auditáveis e rastreáveis. Um dos exemplos mostrados na keynote: um assistente de consolidação financeira que reduz o tempo de fechamento em até 68%.

A Bosch Digital subiu ao palco como cliente early adopter, confirmando que já está testando Joule Work e Joule Studio com feedback positivo.

Construir um agente ficou mais rápido (e mais barato)

A developer keynote trouxe demos ao vivo do Joule Studio — a plataforma para criar agentes de IA da SAP. O destaque: o tempo para ir de uma ideia a um agente funcionando caiu de 13 horas para cerca de 2,5 horas. E nos testes da SAP, o custo por tarefa caiu 50% porque os agentes não precisam adivinhar — eles já conhecem os processos e dados da empresa.

 

O segredo está no SAP Knowledge Graph, que encontra automaticamente as APIs, MCP servers e data products relevantes, e o Joule Studio gera a estrutura e a lógica de integração. Isso abre a construção de agentes para muito além dos programadores tradicionais.

Robôs na fábrica e IA no espaço

 

 

Uma das surpresas do dia foi o anúncio do Physical AI by SAP — a extensão da empresa autônoma para o mundo físico. A Intel mostrou que já opera robôs autônomos no seu site em Chengdu, onde o SAP Warehouse Management dirige os robôs e escreve os resultados de volta no SAP como transações reais.

E o modelo de IA tabular da SAP (SAP-RPT) está literalmente no espaço: rodando a bordo da Estação Espacial Internacional em parceria com a HPE, fazendo previsão de falhas e detectando anomalias em tempo real — sem enviar dados de volta à Terra.

Governança: o que torna a IA escalável

A SAP reforçou que governança não freia a adoção de IA — ela é o que torna a adoção em escala possível. O novo AI Governance Assistant ajuda empresas a atender os requisitos do EU AI Act e estará disponível em novembro para clientes do programa early adopter. Todo agente precisa ser verificado no SAP AI Agent Hub antes de rodar em produção.

E a noite foi de festa

O Day 2 encerrou com a celebração dos 30 anos do SAP TechEd — uma noite temática inspirada nos bairros de Berlim, celebrando três décadas de comunidade, código e inovação.

Ainda dá tempo de assistir

Todo o conteúdo das keynotes e sessões está disponível on demand no SAP TechEd Virtual, que é gratuito. Se você não acompanhou ao vivo, ainda pode assistir tudo no seu ritmo.

entry.title: Can You Run a Space Station? Lessons on Sustainability from the Dubai Museum of the Future
entry.content:
The Metaphor of the Orbiting Outpost
If you step onto Level 2 of the Dubai Museum of the Future, you will encounter the OSS Hope Simulator from SAP. Set against a glowing, interactive console, it presents users with a direct challenge: "Can you run a space station?"
 
To enterprise architects, developers, and consultants, this installation is far more than a visionary gaming experience. A space station operates as a strictly closed system. There is no margin for error; every drop of water, molecule of carbon, and unit of energy must be meticulously logged, tracked, and reused.
This setup mirrors our situation on Earth. Our planet is a closed ecosystem facing finite resource boundaries. The exhibit emphasizes that the exact same real-time data tracking required to sustain life in space is essential to preserving our enterprise ecosystems on Earth.
 
The Three Pillars of a Circular Enterprise
The logic of the simulator relies on keeping three core metrics balanced. These variables map directly to SAP's foundational sustainability pillars:
  • Zero Emissions: Moving beyond simple carbon estimation to active, automated decarbonization across the entire supply chain.
  • Zero Waste: Shifting production models from linear consumption to fully circular material loops where nothing is discarded.
  • Zero Inequalities: Establishing transparent workforce safety, ethical sourcing, and corporate governance down to the last tier of suppliers.
In a space station, you cannot survive without a central ledger to balance these vectors. On Earth, you cannot optimize what you do not accurately count.
 
️ Decoding the Architecture behind the "Wall of Knowledge"
The installation features an interactive "Wall of Knowledge" that showcases real-world global use cases. The simulator's backend logic runs on eight distinct technology domains. Five of these domains form the core foundation of the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) ecosystem:
 
1. Embedded AI & Predictive Forecasting
  • Simulation Mechanics: Dynamically balancing oxygen reserves and predicting machinery failure points before they occur.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Embedding native intelligence via SAP Business AI and SAP Joule to flag supply chain anomalies, forecast emissions spikes, and automate ledger corrections before period-end close.
2. Advanced Real-Time Analytics
  • Simulation Mechanics: Aggregating and visualizing live telemetry across life support, energy grids, and cargo bays.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Ingesting highly disparate IoT and operational data into the high-speed data tier of SAP HANA. This feeds directly into an auditable ESG reporting layer via the SAP Sustainability Control Tower.
 
3. Digital Twins & Simulation Sandboxes
  • Simulation Mechanics: Testing the operational risk of environmental adjustments inside a safe virtual environment first.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Mapping asset management data to live logistics feeds. This allows operations leads to simulate structural facility changes before committing physical resources.
4. Blockchain & Asset Traceability
  • Simulation Mechanics: Verifying the origin, safety, and operational lifecycle of all arriving raw materials.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Utilizing immutable ledger records to verify end-to-end supply chain transparency, ensuring strict compliance with evolving international sustainability regulations.
5. Hyper-Automation
  • Simulation Mechanics: Executing real-time automated adjustments to life support loops to completely eliminate human delay.
  • SAP Enterprise Deployment: Orchestrating touchless business workflows across SAP S/4HANA to dynamically adjust production rates based on resource availability.
The Enterprise Lesson: Profit and Planet on a Single Platform
The ultimate takeaway for the SAP ecosystem is clear: the precision engineering needed to pilot a space station matches the exact methodology required to run a sustainable business.
As technology professionals, the configurations, custom code lines, and system integrations we build on SAP BTP serve as the actual plumbing for global resource consumption. By integrating carbon, waste, and social ledgers directly into our core ERP data structures, we turn abstract sustainability goals into repeatable, daily business operations.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026 — Day 3: O Grand Finale
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 — Day 3: O Grand Finale


E aí, pessoal! Terceiro e último dia de SAP TechEd 2026. Confesso que bateu aquela mistura de "quero mais" com "preciso digerir tudo isso". Acompanhei o evento virtual daqui de Curitiba e, pra quem ficou até o final, o Day 3 trouxe aquele conteúdo que nem sempre vira manchete mas que, na prática, é o que mais muda o dia a dia de quem trabalha com SAP.

Se você caiu de paraquedas aqui, dá uma passada nos posts anteriores. No Day 1 falei do Enterprise AI Gateway, do modelo de IA rodando na Estação Espacial e das novidades pra quem é de ABAP. No Day 2 teve o Kasimir (aquele gato espião que roubou a cena), os 300 agentes prontos, robôs autônomos na fábrica da Intel e a festa dos 30 anos. Agora vamos pro gran finale.

Sem dados bons, não tem IA que salve

Todo mundo fala de agente, de IA generativa, de automação. Mas o Day 3 deixou claro uma coisa: nada disso funciona se os dados da empresa forem uma bagunça. E a SAP parece ter entendido isso.

O SAP Business Data Cloud ganhou um tal de Ontology Manager — basicamente uma ferramenta pra definir como os dados se relacionam entre si, mesmo quando vem de fontes diferentes (SAP e não-SAP). Parece abstrato? Pense assim: é o que permite você perguntar "qual cliente mais comprou no último trimestre?" pro Joule e ele realmente entender a pergunta, porque sabe qual tabela é cliente, qual é pedido e como elas se conectam.

Algo que me chamou atenção: a SAP fechou parceria com a Dremio pra montar um lakehouse dentro do BDC, com suporte a Apache Iceberg e Apache Polaris. Pra quem não é da área de dados, isso significa que dá pra consultar dados de vários repositórios sem copiar nada — o dado fica onde está, você só consulta.

Tem também a expansão do SAP Databricks e a integração com o SAP Reltio (aquela empresa que a SAP comprou em maio) pra master data. Ou seja: a SAP tá montando uma camada de dados que não fica só no mundo SAP. Isso muda o jogo.

O dev ganhou brinquedos novos

Se você é desenvolvedor, esse dia foi pra você.

Primeiro: dá pra construir agentes usando CrewAI e LangGraph direto na BTP. São frameworks open source que a galera já conhece do mundo Python, agora com identidade, autorização e governança da SAP por baixo. Isso é grande. Significa que você não precisa aprender um framework proprietário pra começar — pode usar o que já sabe.

Segundo: a integração com n8n dentro do Joule Studio. Pra quem não conhece, n8n é uma ferramenta de automação de workflows (tipo um Zapier open source). Agora dá pra desenhar workflows visuais e rodar dentro do ambiente SAP. Clientes early adopter já estão testando.

E tem os MCP Servers locais pra CAP, Fiori elements, SAPUI5 e mobile dev kit. Na prática, isso permite que assistentes de código como Cursor, Claude Code, Cline e Windsurf entendam o contexto SAP do seu projeto. Você abre o VS Code, pede pro assistente gerar um serviço CAP e ele já sabe o que é uma entity, uma annotation, um draft.

E o HANA Cloud agora também tem suporte a MCP — agentes podem consultar dados relacionais, espaciais e até fazer busca semântica com vetores. O detalhe legal: o HANA pode servir de memória de longo prazo pros agentes, mantendo contexto entre sessões.

O que vem por aí

Algumas coisas anunciadas ainda não estão disponíveis, então anota aí no calendário:

Até o final de 2026: Joule ganha funcionalidades de administração de banco no HANA Cloud, um modelo de decisão pra tarefas como aprovação de pedidos, e o Sovereign Cloud passa a rodar SAP AI Core e Datasphere no Reino Unido, Austrália e Canadá.

Pro primeiro trimestre de 2027: chega o SAP Enterprise AI Gateway (aquele que centraliza toda a governança de IA), as novas capacidades do Knowledge Graph com dados do cliente, a versão final do SAP-RPT-2.0 com detecção de anomalias, e o lakehouse com Dremio.

E até dezembro desse ano, rodar agentes customizados no runtime do Joule Studio continua gratuito pra clientes selecionados. A certificação de Joule Studio Developer também é free até 31 de dezembro. Se você tá pensando em começar, esse é o momento.

Fechando a mala (virtual)

Três dias de evento é muita coisa. Vou ser honesto: não dá pra absorver tudo em tempo real. Mas o que ficou pra mim foi isso: a SAP não tá mais só falando de IA. Ela tá entregando ferramentas, runtime, governança e uma camada de dados que conecta o mundo SAP com o resto. E abriu o jogo pra frameworks que a comunidade já usa.

Pra quem é de ABAP como eu, o recado é claro: o ABAP não vai morrer, mas vai mudar. MCP Server, VS Code, modelos de IA treinados em código ABAP — quem se adaptar vai surfar essa onda. Quem ficar parado... bom, você já sabe.
